article.title: Using Help
article.content:
There are 4 parts to the {$DP_NAME} help system. These are:

  • {$DP_NAME} Guide - This is the section you are reading now, articles written by {$DP_NAME} staff about using {$DP_NAME}
  • {$DP_NAME} Glossary - These are short descriptions of keywords used in DeskPRO
  • {$DP_NAME} Tooltips - These are tips you will see through the {$DP_NAME} Interface. They are indicated by the blue help icon. They will generally appear on form input or the top right hand corner of the major page sections
  • Collaborative Help - This is help that you and your colleagues will build. Each company uses {$DP_NAME} differently and this section allows you to list your own policies and guides about how to use DeskPRO.

article.title: Creating Users
article.content:
You can create users by filling in a form or by creating many users at once by simply provifing email addresses.

Creatng Users

Select the menu option: Users / Create Users / New User. Using this form, you can create a brand new user. All of the values can be left default or blank except for the Email and Username which you need to specify. It is also a good idea to keep 'Send Welcome Email' to 'Yes' so the user can be notified about their newly created account.

Remember the Notes tab where you can write a note about this user account. For example, why you created it manually instead of having the user do so.

Creating Many Users

To create many users at once, selecct the menu otion: Users / Create Users / Mass Create Users. Using this form, you only need to supply a list of email addresses. Everything else will be gathered automatically including the Useranme (which will just be based off of the email address).

article.title: Finding Users
article.content: To search for a user, select the menu option: Users / Find Users. Using this form you can search on almost any piece of information that is tied to a user. From the most basic and broad searches like the state of their validation, or something specific like an email address or user ID.

article.title: Deleting Users
article.content:
To delete a user, you fist must be viewing their profile. To get to their profile you can search for them via the Find Users form (see the other help article on how to search for users) or by following a link in one of their tickets in the User Properties tab.

On their profile page click the 'Delete User' link at the bottom of the User Properties tab. Please note that when you delete a user, all information associated with the user will be deleted. This includes their Knowlegebase subscriptions, their tickets, tracked emails, user notes etc.

article.title: Creating Tickets
article.content:
To create a ticket, select the menu option Tickets / Start New Ticket. You have the option of either searching for a user the ticket should belong to, or creating a brand new user.

After you have chosen a user (or chosen to create a user), the New Ticket form will appear. Please note that the main message box you see in the General Options tab will be your reply. If the ticket is to be in response to a question (for example, a user asked via a different method of cumminication like telephone or instant messaging) then enter the question into the message area in the User Message tab.

article.title: Finding Tickets
article.content:
You can search for a ticket by selecting the menu option Tickets / Find Tickets. This form lets you enter as much or as little critera as you need, and will display the tickets matching the critera on the next page.

You can also choose to save a search as a Saved Search so you can run it quickly next time you need to search for the same thing. To do this, you simply need to check the Create Saved Search checkbox under the search form and enter a name for your saved search. You can run saved searches directly from the top bar using the Run Search select box.

article.title: Deleting Tickets
article.content:
You can delete a ticket by first viewing the ticket, and then selecting the Delete Ticket option from the Perform Action select box at the top of the page.

Alternatively, you can delete a ticket right from the search results page. First check the checkbox for the ticket row, then choose Delete Ticket from the select box at the bottom of the page and press the Go button. You can delete multiple tickets this way by just checking the ones you wish to delete.

article.title: Mass Ticket Processing
article.content:
You can manage multiple tickets at a time right from the results page after you perform a search. Beside each ticket, there is a [+] that you can use to reveal a select box with certain actions you can perform, as well as a quick reply box.

After you have chosen all the actions you want to perform on the tickets, and any replies you want to add, be sure to click the Go button at the bottom of the listing so the actions are perfomed.

article.title: Quick Replies
article.content:
Quick replies (also known as 'canned replies') help you save time by removing the need for you to type out the same replies over and over again. All you need to do is type them once, and then you can insert the reply into the reply box and submit the message.

Creating and Managing Quick Replies
To manage your quick replies, choose the menu option Tickets / Quick Replies. This will allow you to create or edit replies and categories. Note that you can also use variables within your quick reply to make them specialized for the ticket. For example, you can insert the users name or the title of the ticket.

Using Quick Replies
When viewing a ticket, you can easily enter the reply text right into the textarea by selecting a reply from the select box to the right, then clicking the Insert into Reply button. Note that this does not submit the form, it just inserts the text into your reply. This allows you to add or change the reply as much as you need, possibly adding multiple quick replies to the same message.

Alternatively, you can add a reply using the Mass Ticket Processing features (see the other {$DP_NAME} Guide page for more information). Just select the Reply with quick reply action and then a quick reply. This method does not allow you to edit the text, if you need more information or need to write a proper reply you should open the ticket.

article.title: Ticket Views
article.content:
Ticket views let you define what information you want to see when ticket search results are displayed. For example, you might want to create a simple view that only shows the title and description instead of the full, detailed view.

To create or edit your views, select the menu item Tickets / Ticket Views. To apply a view to your current search results, you can choose it from the select box on the top right corner and click the Update View button.

article.title: Save Tickets
article.content:
Sometimes you might want to save a ticket so you can easily come back to it later. {$DP_NAME} lets you save tickets to your own personal collection.

Adding a Ticket
There are two ways to save a ticket. The first is by viewing the ticket and selecting the Save Ticket option from the Perform Action select box at the top of the page.

Alternatively, if you already haev the ticket ID or ticket reference number, you can go to your saved tickets page (Tickets / Saved Tickets) and click on Add Tickets. Fill in the form and submit it to add the ticket to your collection.

Getting to your saved tickets
To view your saved tickets, you can select the menu option Tickets / Saved Tickets. This will list all of the tickets you have in your collection and let you delete them if you need to. Clicking on the subject line will take you to the ticket page.

If you are using the framed interface, you can also get to your saved tickets by clicking on the Searchess tab and selecting one from the select box.
